title: Scheduled Tasks
summary: Enable scheduling, choose a time rule, and handle restarts and multiple instances.

sources.title: Engineering Digest: Ultimate Guide to Scheduling Tasks with Cron Jobs in Spring Boot
Engineering Digest: Adding Sentiment to Journal App

richText: Run a method on a schedule
@Scheduled asks Spring to call a bean method according to a time rule.
Add @EnableScheduling to a configuration class to enable scheduled methods.
A normal scheduled method takes no arguments. Spring does not use its return value.
The application must be running when the scheduled time arrives.
fixedDelay waits for the previous execution to finish, then waits for the configured delay.
fixedRate uses a fixed interval between scheduled start times. A busy scheduler can start work later.
cron uses a calendar rule, such as every Sunday at 09:00.
Spring cron has six fields in this order: second, minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week.
The zone attribute selects the timezone used for the cron expression.

example.title: Queue a weekly digest on Sunday
description: Use Spring Boot 3, Spring Framework 6, and Java 17.
WeeklyDigestService is an application service that calculates and queues summaries. Its implementation is separate from the timing rule.
explanation: 0 0 9 * * SUN selects Sunday at 09:00:00 in Asia/Kolkata.
Spring calls queueDigests, which delegates to aggregateAndQueue.
The annotation cannot run while the application is stopped.

richText: @Scheduled does not save job history or replay missed executions automatically.
Store pending work in a database if it must survive restarts.
Each application instance has its own scheduler. Two instances can start the same job.
Use a shared lock or a dedicated scheduler when only one instance should start a job.
A unique job-and-period record can prevent duplicate work for the same reporting period.
Set timeouts for database and network work. Record which items failed so they can be retried separately.
